## Observation
When `REBAR_ROOT` is unset, every library read rediscovers the code repo root with `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, through `repo_root` (`src/rebar/_config_sources.py:53`), which `config.tracker_dir` and `config.load_config` call on each read. Measured on a throwaway two-repo store with the freshness marker fresh, after the synonymous-destined-cricket fix:

- `rebar.show_ticket`: 5 git spawns. 2 come from `_reads._tracker` → `config.tracker_dir` (one direct, one via `load_config`), 2 from the same path in the cross-session warning's own read, and 1 from `cross_session.cross_session_warning_for` → `load_config`.
- `rebar.list_tickets`: 2 git spawns (`tracker_dir` and `load_config`).

With `REBAR_ROOT` set, or an explicit `repo_root` (as `rebar audit serve` passes), the same reads spawn 0. The root of a process's cwd does not change between reads in one process, so these are repeated lookups of the same answer.

Discovered while fixing synonymous-destined-cricket (40c3-d22a-3872-4c8c), whose scope is the freshness throttle only.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A library `show_ticket` with `REBAR_ROOT` unset, run from inside a git work tree, starts at most 1 `rev-parse --show-toplevel`, shown by a git-spawn-count test.
- [x] A cwd change between reads still resolves the new cwd's repo root, shown by a test.
